title: Tratzberg Castle Stans
name: Tratzberg Castle Stans
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Tratzberg in Stans in the Inntal: late Gothic Renaissance castle from 1500 with the Habsburger-Saal, armory, and interactive children's audio drama tour.
beschreibung:
Overview

The magnificent Schloss Tratzberg is perched on a wooded rocky ridge high above the Inntal in the Tyrolean municipality of Stans in the Schwaz district at an altitude of around 620 metres. Picturesquely situated between Jenbach and Schwaz at the foothills of the Karwendelgebirge, the fortified complex is considered one of the best-preserved and architecturally most significant late Renaissance castles in the entire European Alpine region. With its artful courtyards, lavishly decorated state rooms, and over 500 years of continuous aristocratic history, this historic monument offers a fascinating journey back in time to the era of the Habsburgs and the Fugger family.

History & Habsburger-Saal

The original Veste Tratzberg was built in the 13th century as a border fortification against Bavaria and was largely destroyed by a devastating fire in the late 15th century. In 1499, the wealthy Schwaz silver mining merchants Veit-Jakob and Simon Tänzl acquired the ruins and transformed them in just eight years into a masterpiece of late Gothic and early Renaissance architecture. In the 16th century, the castle came into the possession of the powerful Augsburg merchant family Fugger, who enriched the palas with splendid Renaissance wooden ceilings and wall paintings. Since 1847, the estate has been owned by the Grafen Enzenberg, who still inhabit the castle today and lovingly preserve it. The absolute centerpiece of the tour is the world-famous Habsburger-Saal: across a 46-metre-long wall surface extends a monumental genealogical tree fresco of the dynasty of Emperor Maximilian I featuring 148 life-size figures of rulers. Further highlights include the Königszimmer, the Gothic castle chapel, the richly furnished Jagdzimmer, and the historic Rüstkammer with original 15th- and 16th-century tournament armor.

Visit & Getting There

Schloss Tratzberg can be visited during the summer months from early April to early November daily from 10:00 to 16:00 on guided tours. The tour is conducted using state-of-the-art audio guides in nine languages (children enjoy an exciting fairy-tale audio drama tour). Admission prices (season 2025/2026): adults approx. €15.50, seniors approx. €14.00, children and teenagers (aged 4 to 17) approx. €9.00, family ticket approx. €39.00. From the castle car park in the valley, the historic slow train Tratzberg-Express travels up to the castle gate (combi-ticket or approx. 20-minute walk through the forest). Getting there by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Schwaz or Jenbach, continuing on the B171 to Stans, following signs to Schloss Tratzberg (large free car park at the Schlosswirt). By public transport: ÖBB/S-Bahn to Jenbach station or Stans bei Schwaz, from there a short walk or regional bus.

Tips

The castle courtyard, the castle restaurant Schlosswirt Tratzberg, and the slow train are accessible with low barriers; the tour through the historical floors of the castle involves some steps. Stop by the shaded beer garden of the Schlosswirt and enjoy traditional Tyrolean dumpling dishes while the children explore the large adventure playground.
